speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked	the Minister for Defence (a) whether the Ministry has determined (i) how the used SAF uniforms came into the possession of the smugglers who were caught unloading them near Batam in November 2016 and (ii) the motive for smuggling the uniforms to Batam; and (b) how does the Ministry intend to prevent such incidents from happening again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: National Servicemen (NSmen) will be reminded to dispose of their old uniforms only via authorised collection points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: These measures will reduce opportunities for unauthorised vendors to obtain and then sell used SAF uniforms.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Could I please ask him to answer part (a) of my question?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does SAF carry out any regular audits or spot checks to ensure that proper disposal is always carried out by the contractors?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What actions will be taken to improve the current disposal process?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What actions will be taken against the persons found responsible for causing or contributing to the uniforms being sold or smuggled into Indonesia?

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: As mentioned earlier, the collection points are all available at all SAF eMarts.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, the point is, we will continue to engage and remind our Servicemen and NSmen on where they should dispose of their used uniforms.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We will ensure that should there be any individuals who have been found to have violated some of these regulations or procedures, they will be taken to task.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Could I ask again what actions will be taken against the persons found responsible for causing or contributing to the uniforms being sold or smuggled into Indonesia?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Another supplementary question, given the answers that the Senior Minister of State has given, is or will Singapore be working with the Indonesian authorities to identify the persons who have been arrested or detained in Indonesia in connection with the investigation for the smuggling of these uniforms?

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I think it is premature to even discuss what actions we will take.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We will look at the situation as it emerges.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Could the Senior Minister of State please share with the House what would be the likely or expected timeline for the investigation to complete such that the Ministry of Defence would be able to consider whether actions will be taken against the persons responsible?

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I think I am not in a position to set any timeline because, ideally, it is up to the Indonesian authorities, and we will leave it to them.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: When they complete the investigation and they share the information with us, then we will take the action accordingly.
